title: Durrani Empire
capsule: The Durrani Empire was founded by Ahmad Shah Abdali (later Durrani, 'Pearl of Pearls') in October 1747 following the assassination of Nader Shah, when a loya jirga of Pashtun chiefs at Kandahar elected him ruler. At its peak the empire stretched from Khorasan (including Mashhad) westward to Nishapur, east to Kashmir and the Punjab, and south to Sindh and Balochistan, making it the largest Muslim polity in Asia at the time. Ahmad Shah led nine invasions of the Indian subcontinent, most decisively defeating the Maratha Confederacy at the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761). Centrifugal pressures — Sikh expansion in the Punjab, Persian recoveries in Khorasan, and dynastic succession disputes — progressively stripped outlying territories; by the dataset's terminal year of 1827 the empire had contracted to the Afghan core under Dost Mohammad Khan's emerging Barakzai rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Afghan core and major provincial capitals are documented by Persian-language chronicles and 18th-century travel accounts; tributary zones in Sindh, Balochistan, and eastern Khorasan are based on military campaign narratives rather than administrative demarcations, and the outer frontier is substantially conjectural.
